entry.title: Review 'Add a self-contained Smithware Factory v3 demo page'
entry.content:
Pull request: https://github.com/guildaidev/experimental/pull/287
Slack thread: https://guild-ai-group.slack.com/archives/C0C411XJV8S/p1790220422323079

Reading order

  1. Self-contained demo page and README entry: docs/smithware-factory-e2e-v3/index.html, README.md
    The HTML file is the entire change; the README row is its only documentation. They are one logical addition.

Areas of concern

  • docs/smithware-factory-e2e-v3/index.html, lines 1006-1030: Check that calling reset() inside simulate() before the run starts cannot fire while a previous run's scheduled timers are still live, producing two concurrent advance() loops. simulate() calls reset() which calls clearTimers() and sets running=false, but if the user clicks Simulate again while a gate btn.addEventListener is still attached (gates are not timer-based and not cleared by clearTimers()), the old gate handler will still resolve and call its done() closure, advancing the stale idx into the new run's STEPS array.
  • docs/smithware-factory-e2e-v3/index.html, lines 1063-1085: Verify the gate click handler is correctly cleaned up on reset. buildSteps() replaces the DOM, so the old btn reference the closure holds becomes detached — but the event listener is already removed by removeEventListener before done() fires, so confirm there is no path where the listener survives a reset and fires against the new DOM. The gate handler is a named function removed on first click, but reset() rebuilds the DOM mid-flight without explicitly aborting pending gate state. If reset() is called after the gate is shown but before the button is clicked, the new DOM has a fresh button with no listener; the old detached button's listener is never removed. This is benign for correctness but worth confirming explicitly.
